description:
Jal Jeevan Mission is a flagship program initiated by the Government of India on August 1, 2019. 

The mission aims to provide safe and adequate drinking water supply through individual household tap connections to all rural households by the year 2024. 

The program is a part of the larger vision of the Government of India to ensure water security and promote sustainable water management practices. 

The primary objective of Jal Jeevan Mission is to ensure that every rural household has access to a functional tap water connection. 

As of October 2023, the target is to provide tap water connections to over 19 crore rural households across India. 

The mission also aims to enhance the quality of drinking water and promote the sustainability of water sources. 

The program emphasizes community participation in the planning, implementation, and management of water supply systems. 

The benefits of the Jal Jeevan Mission are substantial. 

Each household that receives a tap water connection will have access to a minimum of 55 liters of water per person per day. 

The estimated cost of providing tap water connections under this mission is approximately ₹3.60 lakh crores over a period of five years. 

The central government contributes 90 percent of the funding for the Union Territories and 50 percent for the states. 

States are expected to contribute the remaining amount based on their financial capabilities. 

The mission also focuses on the quality of water supplied, ensuring that it meets the standards set by the Bureau of Indian Standards. 

In terms of eligibility, the scheme targets all rural households, particularly those that are currently unserved or underserved in terms of water supply. 

There are no specific age limits or educational requirements for beneficiaries. 

However, households that are part of marginalized communities such as Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes are prioritized. 

The application process for Jal Jeevan Mission is designed to be straightforward and community-driven. 

Villagers can express their need for a tap water connection through local Gram Panchayats. 

The Gram Panchayat will then compile a list of households requiring connections and submit it to the relevant district authorities. 

Required documents typically include proof of residence and identification of the household head. 

Once the application is approved, the implementation of the water supply system begins. 

The timeline for the implementation of the mission is set to be completed by 2024. 

As of October 2023, significant progress has been made with over 11 crore tap connections provided to rural households. 

The mission has also established a robust monitoring framework to ensure transparency and accountability in the implementation process. 

The Ministry of Jal Shakti is the primary implementing authority for the Jal Jeevan Mission. 

The ministry works in collaboration with state governments and local bodies to ensure effective execution of the program. 

Each state has a dedicated water supply and sanitation department responsible for the mission's implementation at the state level. 

The mission also encourages the use of technology for better management and monitoring of water supply systems. 

Mobile applications and online portals have been developed to facilitate real-time tracking of water supply and complaints. 

Community participation is a critical aspect of the Jal Jeevan Mission. 

Local Water and Sanitation Committees are formed to involve community members in the management of water supply systems. 

These committees are responsible for the operation and maintenance of water supply infrastructure. 

The mission also promotes awareness and education regarding water conservation and hygiene practices. 

As part of the mission, the government has allocated funds for the construction of water supply infrastructure such as pipelines, storage tanks, and treatment plants. 

The mission also includes provisions for the rejuvenation of traditional water bodies and groundwater recharge. 

In addition to providing tap water connections, the mission aims to improve the overall water supply infrastructure in rural areas. 

The Jal Jeevan Mission is expected to have a significant impact on public health by reducing waterborne diseases. 

Access to safe drinking water is crucial for improving the quality of life in rural areas. 

The mission also aligns with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, particularly Goal 6, which aims to ensure availability and sustainable management of water and sanitation for all. 

The government has set up a dedicated helpline for beneficiaries to address their queries and complaints regarding the mission. 

This helpline is accessible through multiple channels including phone calls and online platforms. 

The mission has received positive feedback from various stakeholders including local communities and NGOs. 

The government is continuously monitoring the progress of the mission through regular assessments and evaluations. 

As of October 2023, several states have achieved significant milestones in providing tap water connections. 

For instance, states like Gujarat and Rajasthan have reported over 90 percent coverage in rural areas. 

The mission has also received recognition at various national and international forums for its innovative approach to water supply management. 

The Jal Jeevan Mission is a transformative initiative that seeks to change the landscape of rural water supply in India. 

By ensuring access to safe drinking water, the mission aims to empower rural communities and improve their overall well-being. 

The government is committed to achieving the goals of the Jal Jeevan Mission within the stipulated timeline. 

As the mission progresses, it is expected to create a lasting impact on rural livelihoods and economic development. 

The success of the Jal Jeevan Mission will serve as a model for future water supply initiatives in India. 

The mission reflects the government's commitment to addressing the critical issue of water scarcity in rural areas. 

Through collaborative efforts and community engagement, the Jal Jeevan Mission aims to create a sustainable and resilient water supply system for all rural households in India.
